verdict.explanation: The observed source1 physical pilot, cached-source0 batch exit0, and explicitly partial aggregate support the exercised happy paths, and the aggregation code preserves the specified weights, complex orders, blocks, and coverage distinctions. Three patch-introduced defects remain in scientific compatibility admission, checkpoint directory durability, and exceptional worker shutdown/accounting; these are static findings, not claims that the supplied numerical results are wrong.

findings.title: Bind scientific helper compatibility at both case admission points
findings.body: If a scientific change is made only in full_noise_probe_inputs.py, original_noise_source.py, cached_mode_source0.py, or an imported physical/projection helper, this binding_contract remains unchanged. reusable() consequently accepts earlier successful generations, and load_case() never checks the recorded implementation lists or a scientific operator/projection compatibility identity; the same unchecked loader also admits explicit --done inputs during final aggregation. A resumed batch can therefore mix sectors evaluated with incompatible force or covariance definitions while reporting complete coverage. Carry and validate a scientific compatibility identity through the producer, reuse, and aggregation boundaries, covering those helpers; preserve explicitly established compatibility for metadata-only edits rather than blindly invalidating old valid data for every recorded file-byte change.

findings.title: Persist checkpoint directory entries before accepting completion
findings.body: The producer fsyncs result.json and done.json file contents but never fsyncs their containing case directory. The runner's later outcome/accepted writes fsync the generation directory, not case/, so they do not establish durability of those two checkpoint names. A host crash can therefore lose a supposedly committed completion and cause a completed physical sector to be recomputed. Fresh generation/run directories likewise are created without syncing the directories containing their new names. Fsync the directories whose entries are published, including the case result/done entries and newly created checkpoint-directory ancestors, before declaring the work durable.

findings.title: Stop and drain active cases before executor shutdown
findings.body: When a parent-side exception escapes the scheduling/readout loop while another case is active, for example an OSError from the fsynced progress write or a rejection receipt write, the ThreadPoolExecutor context exits before this outer handler sets stop. Its __exit__ waits for workers, so live physical producers continue until their own timeout, batch deadline, or normal completion instead of being stopped on the parent failure. The loop is then abandoned without consuming the remaining futures, so even successfully written child outcomes are absent from the run's completed/cost accounting. Set stop and drain/reconcile active futures inside the executor scope on exceptional exits, before its blocking shutdown.

actual_cached_source0_batch.notes: Intent binds the producer/runner/aggregator/Python, original inputs, and paid packets; argv pins CPU7 through taskset and every listed BLAS/OpenMP override is1. Outcome binds 839-byte stdout and empty stderr; progress records start, complete, then exit. static_contract_results: Each launched record gets generation-UUID and a nonexistent case child; files use exclusive creation and originals are never overwritten or removed.

The normal subprocess path persists intent before spawn, fsyncs stdout/stderr, wait4-reaps the direct producer, writes outcome, then reloads it before consuming done/result. Result-only files and unsuccessful exits are not accepted by batch reuse.

load_case authenticates the result bytes/SHA/path through sibling done.json, requires complete schema/status, literal unweighted [0,1] modes, and checks source/preparation/frame/raw-D/selection/model and original spin/internal-k identity against the bound original inputs.

load_context requires all128 unique original slot identities and exact1/64 slot weights; aggregate rejects repeated original records and repeated explicit spin/internal-k pairs, requires indices0..127 for complete, and requires both spins on the same64 mesh for full coverage.

parse_covariance requires the four distinct ordered mode pairs and four distinct retained/omitted blocks for each. aggregate multiplies each raw complex full/block/defect by its sector weight once, retains AB and BA separately, and performs no partial renormalization, extra spin multiplication, spatial division, symmetrization, PSD repair, or clipping.

The normal timeout/SIGINT/SIGTERM path sets stop or a termination reason, sends SIGKILL to the child's process group, then waits for its own PID. Bounded workers use separate CPU slots with BLAS/OpenMP capped at1. Exceptional parent shutdown has the separate reported defect.

Normal child failures preserve their generations, produce rejection records, list failed sectors, and mark partial physical-action counts unknown. Unstarted records are separately computed as requested minus completed minus launched; incomplete records include failed/missing work. Unfinished in-case force arrays are not claimed resumable.
Only one compatible committed generation per record can be reused; multiple compatible generations cause an explicit ambiguity error instead of silent selection.

Resume skip, rejected-generation recovery, duplicate-input rejection, child failure/OOM, wall/case timeout, SIGINT/SIGTERM, and exceptional-parent-error behavior were inspected statically, not exercised by this reviewer.
No host-crash/fsync fault experiment was performed. The durability finding follows from the publication calls and missing directory synchronization, not an observed loss in the supplied artifacts.

No incompatible helper update was executed. The compatibility finding establishes that both admission paths omit the scientific compatibility check; it does not assert that source0 or source1 is presently scientifically incompatible.

Recorded packet/artifact SHA256 and byte bindings are reproduced as existing evidence; this review did not independently rehash original numerical banks or source files, and does not claim new binary banking.
